newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NSW exports over 1 MT Australia wheat in Feb.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NSW exports over 1 MT Australia wheat in Feb.

text.p: The New South Wales (NSW) division of the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) had set a new record by exporting more than one million tonnes exports of wheat in February, state manager Ted Laskie said in a statement.
"This is a remarkable achievement," he said.
Nationally, the AWB exported 1.8 million tonnes in December and a staggering 2.1 million tonnes in January, he said.
AWB was attempting to break the record again with expected exports from NSW alone of more than one million tonnes in both February and March, he said.
High-level exports were being achieved through a well-managed front-ended shipping programme to maximise movements out of the country in record time, he said.
The object, with the current massive crop, was to move as much grain offshore as quickly as possible, he said.
Rapid exports allowed the AWB to capture current opportune price levels before the Northern Hemisphere harvest, which generally occurred in the May/June period, he said.
Prices in those months tended to soften because of increased availability of grain on the market, he said.
The largest sale of grain from NSW this season had been almost 250,000 tonnes to Egypt, he said.
Sales to Indonesia and Thailand followed closely behind.
NSW growers this season produced a mostly good quality crop, with less categories needed to be received into the storage system. This had made it easier to export, he said.
The forecast pool price of A$170.00-A$180.00 a tonne for 1997/98 Australian Standard White wheat was a solid return, he said.
